target_customer: Retail investors reading free news, with subscription and syndication to publishers and financial institutions planned
problem: SEC filings contain newsworthy facts that are hard for ordinary readers to parse, so MarketBrief turned them into plain English news stories automatically.
business_model: freemium subscription ($9 per month after 10 free articles) plus planned syndication

founders.name: Chris Auer
founders.background_notes: Only founder on the YC page; bio not given.

founders.name: Jason Zucchetto
founders.background_notes: Named as founder in the August 2011 TechCrunch article and quoted as co-founder by IR Magazine.

founders.name: Michael Shafrir
founders.background_notes: Named as a founder in the August 2011 TechCrunch article only.

competitors.name: Wall Street Journal and CNNMoney
competitors.what: Established financial news outlets that MarketBrief said it hoped to compete with more directly over time

technical_complexity.rationale: Parsing roughly half of the SEC's 500 filing types into readable stories with some human review (TechCrunch, August 2011) was real text engineering for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Filings are public and story templates can be rebuilt; the claimed edge was cross checking earlier filings for context.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source describes what incumbents did.

market_need_then: IR Magazine in August 2011 reported about 110,000 monthly visitors, mostly retail investors, which shows some audience demand; the same piece doubted investor relations officers used it.

branding.domain_note: Company site was marketbrief.com per the YC page; an earlier product name was SECWatch (secwatch.com). A 1991 MARKETBRIEF trademark by an unrelated owner is abandoned. Domain history not found.

identity.logo: not described in any source found

rebrands.why: not stated; TechCrunch (August 2011) says the service launched in 2009 as SECWatch

brand_strength.rationale: Generic compound name resembling MarketWatch and Briefing.com, and no source shows brand recognition.

outcome_analysis: MarketBrief automated plain English stories from SEC filings and reached about 110,000 monthly visitors by August 2011 with a $9 per month paywall, but no funding round, exit or shutdown account was found, so the cause of its inactive status is not public. The audience was mostly retail investors rather than paying institutions.
notes: marketbrief.com returned HTTP 503 so the site is treated as unavailable. Outcome and funding searches found nothing, so the cause of inactivity is not public. Narrative Science was seen as a possible rival but no source ties it to SEC filing news, so it is not listed. The founder list rests on one TechCrunch article for Zucchetto and Shafrir; the YC page lists only Auer.
